fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. Esther, the queen, has no summons and walks into that court anyway. The text says that as soon as the king saw her standing there, "…she found favor in his sight." (Esther 5:2) Going in unsummoned could mean death (Esther 4:11), so finding favor in his sight is exactly what she needs in that moment.

Close to the royal stuff, friend, but not quite. The text says the king extended "…the gold scepter in his hand toward Esther…" and she touched its tip (Esther 5:2). A crown isn't part of that moment, because it's the scepter.

Exactly right, baker. The king asks, "What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be given to you." (Esther 5:3) He says it right there in the court, to Esther. Half a kingdom is quite an offer.

That sounds generous, friend, but the king says something different. He says, "What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be given to you." (Esther 5:3) No provinces are named, just up to half the kingdom.

Mordecai, Esther's cousin (Esther 2:7), is the one who urged her to go to the king (Esther 4:7-8), so I see why he came to mind. But Esther doesn't ask for anything about him here. She says, "If it pleases the king, may the king and Haman come today to the banquet I have prepared for the king." (Esther 5:4) The only thing on her request list is the banquet.

I see why Mordecai came to mind, friend, since he's Esther's cousin (Esther 2:7) and part of the whole situation. But the text never has her ask for him to join them. She says, "…may the king and Haman come tomorrow to the banquet I will prepare for them." (Esther 5:8) Her answer is a second invitation.

That would be a different move, baker, but it's the opposite of what Esther does. She keeps Haman on the guest list and says, "…may the king and Haman come tomorrow to the banquet I will prepare for them." (Esther 5:8) Haman isn't sent anywhere, he's invited back. Then she says she will answer the king's question.

That's right, baker. The text says Mordecai, Esther's cousin (Esther 2:7), "…did not rise or tremble in fear at his presence." (Esther 5:9) Haman was walking out full of joy, and Mordecai just stays put. I think it was a very quiet kind of standoff.
That's not what the text says, friend. Mordecai, Esther's cousin (Esther 2:7), "…did not rise or tremble in fear at his presence." (Esther 5:9) There's no bowing in this verse.

That's a reasonable guess, baker, but the text doesn't have Mordecai walking away. It says he "…did not rise or tremble in fear at his presence." (Esther 5:9) Mordecai is Esther's cousin (Esther 2:7), and here he's at the king's gate, not getting up.

I can see why you'd think so, baker, since Haman is filled with rage (Esther 5:9). But the text says, "Nevertheless, Haman restrained himself and went home." (Esther 5:10) He restrains himself and heads home from the gate. So the card's claim isn't what the text says.

That's right, friend. After the gallows advice, Zeresh and his friends add, "Then go to the banquet with the king and enjoy yourself." (Esther 5:14) They hand Haman the plan and tell him to enjoy himself. The banquet is still on the calendar.
